text:
Raj: heads-up, seeing recurring XID spikes + ECC correctable flurry on rack Z-7 GPUs since 02:00 UTC. 6 different cards across 3 hosts. :rotating_light:
Sophia: on it, can you paste the kernel logs and pci resets?
Raj: yes, short tail: `Mar 12 02:03:12 host-z7-03 kernel: NVRM: Xid (0000:3f): 31, PID=4128`
Raj: also `EDAC MC0: ECC error detected on GPU 0, channel 2`
Nate: interesting pattern, all affected GPUs are A40s with board rev B1 from the same procurement batch.
Elena: are these the nodes we swapped last quarter? memory binning note?
Chris: quick check: network uplinks for the rack show brief 10Gb link flaps around the same times - could cause partial IO storms + reset cascades.
Raj: link flaps + XID correlation noted. I kicked a `drain` on host-z7-03 and z7-07, moved jobs off.
ops-bot: host-z7-03 status -> draining (jobs migrated), nv_peer_count=0, health=degraded
Amanda: good. We should quarantine the remaining cards on hosts z7-01..z7-09 until we confirm root cause. That reduces capacity ~9 GPUs in the pool. Thoughts on immediate mitigation?
Sophia: short-term: mark rack Z-7 as low-priority for scheduling and enable conservative batching (max_batch=4) for any remaining nodes to reduce burst IO.
Nate: vendor-notify-bot, can you trigger an RMA start? Suspect bad batch; need serial capture + voltage logs.
vendor-notify-bot: RMA ticket created #RMA-9821. Please attach `dmesg`, nvml logs, and vendor-requested serial list. ETA vendor ack 4-6 hrs.
Chris: for triage: plan A = firmware rollback to 534 on one isolated host and run 24h burn; plan B = vendor swap if rollback doesn't lower XID rate.
Elena: also schedule an IR probe: run `pcirescan && stress-ng --gpu 0 --timeout 2h` on a canary node after firmware change. Keep telemetry on.
Raj: I'm attaching the small perf/telemetry summary in the ticket and listing serials. Copying `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,serial,board_id,ecc.mode --format=csv` output.
Amanda: ops impact: losing 9 GPUs is ~6% of peak capacity for west-1 cluster this hour. I'll kick cost/priority notification to platform teams.
Sophia: who will coordinate the physical RMA if vendor asks for returns? ops oncall or Nate?
Nate: I can do staging pickup; coordinate with supply chain for replacements to be shipped to our staging lab (do not send back to cloud colo).
Chris: if vendor determines it's batch-level, request cross-rack serial check—we may have 2 more affected racks with same PO.
Raj: agreed. Immediate next steps: 1) quarantine remaining Z-7 GPUs (Amanda) 2) schedule firmware rollback + 24h burn on canary host (Chris & Elena) 3) vendor RMA ticket (Nate) 4) update capacity routing to prefer other racks (Sophia). I'll update ticket with logs and keep thread posted.
Amanda: done on quarantine label and updated scheduler tags.
ops-bot: scheduler update applied: rack Z-7 -> node-selector:avoid=true
vendor-notify-bot: vendor acknowledged #RMA-9821, requested additional thermal telemetry.
Raj: adding thermal traces. If we see any thermal anomalies we escalate to emergency RMA.
Elena: one more ask — capture PCIe error counters with `lspci -vvv` and `/sys/kernel/debug/pci_reserve` dump before nodes fully cold-boot.
Sophia: noted. I'll also post a short explainer in #infra-status to warn infra consumers about lower west-1 capacity.
Nate: will pick up replacements to lab if vendor approves. ETA 48-72 hrs after vendor approval.
Chris: after canary passes we'll reintroduce nodes with `--no-burst` then slowly ramp. Documenting the rollout steps in the ticket.
Raj: thanks all. If XID spikes continue on canary, escalate to postmortem immediately. :thinking_face:
